fields.name: taxAuthorityName
fields.label: Tax Authority Name
fields.sourceQuote: Type a unique name (generally the country name) for the tax authority.
fields.notes: General step of the New Tax Authority wizard (Tax Authorities tab). No length constraint documented.

fields.name: taxAuthorityCountry
fields.label: Country
fields.sourceQuote: Select the associated country.
fields.notes: General step. The corpus never enumerates the country list. Cross-cutting constraint: supported-countries-for-vat-8b38bab8.md names UK/Japan/Australia as primary supported and says US, Canada, India and other multi-tax countries are NOT supported, while the tools-guides topics canada-de22c9f9.md and uk-us-japan-australia-0557084a.md give full US and Canada VAT field implementations. Contradiction recorded, not reconciled.

fields.name: taxAuthorityStateProvince
fields.label: State/Province
fields.sourceQuote: Select the associated states/provinces in the list.
fields.notes: General step. Leaving it empty applies the tax authority to the whole country: 'If the tax authority applies to the entire country, do not select any states/provinces.' Feeds the Company Locations ship-to comparison.

fields.name: taxAuthorityTaxName
fields.label: Tax Name
fields.sourceQuote: Type a tax name, up to five characters maximum.
fields.notes: Five-character maximum is the only documented length constraint on the page. step-3-access-tax-authorities-2fae4ae3.md gives GST, MwST and VAT as EXAMPLES of typical tax names - examples, not an enumerated value set, so no validValues are recorded.

fields.name: taxRateTypeName
fields.label: Tax Rate Type Name
fields.sourceQuote: Type the name of the rate, for example, Standard or Reduced.
fields.notes: Tax Rate Types step. 'Standard'/'Reduced' are stated as examples, and tax-administration-tool-0f5fff3c.md gives 'exempt, standard, or reduced' also as examples - neither is a documented value list, so validValues stays empty deliberately.

fields.name: taxRateTypeCalculationMethod
fields.label: Calculation Method
fields.sourceQuote: Select Percentage. This is the default choice.
fields.notes: Tax Rate Types step. Percentage is the ONLY documented choice and is called the default; the corpus never names a second calculation method. Do not infer one.

fields.name: taxRateRateType
fields.label: Rate Type
fields.sourceQuote: Select the rate type.
fields.notes: Tax Rates step. Values are the Tax Rate Types created in the previous wizard step, so the list is tenant-created, not enumerable from documentation. Selecting a type reveals Tax Percent.

fields.name: taxRateEffectiveDate
fields.label: Effective Date
fields.sourceQuote: Enter the start date for the rate.
fields.notes: Tax Rates step. Date format not documented.

fields.name: taxRateTaxPercent
fields.label: Tax Percent
fields.sourceQuote: This field appears by default and is based on the Percentage calculation method. Enter the percentage here.
fields.notes: Tax Rates step. Conditional field - appears only after Rate Type is selected, and its presence is tied to the Percentage calculation method.

fields.name: taxAuthoritiesList
fields.label: Tax Authorities (list)
fields.sourceQuote: The following information appears for any existing tax authorities.
fields.notes: Read-only grid on the Tax Authorities tab with columns Tax Authority, Country, State/Province, Tax Name. Not an input control; recorded so the automation can read existing authorities. 'This is the states/province associated with the tax authority.'

fields.name: expenseTypeGroupTaxAuthorityFilter
fields.label: Tax Authority
fields.sourceQuote: On the Expense Types Group tab, select from the Tax Authority list.
fields.notes: Tab-level selector that scopes every expense type group. Values are the tax authorities configured on the Tax Authorities tab. NOTE the tab label contradiction: this file calls it 'Expense Types Group tab', the-basic-process-12a5686d.md calls it 'Expense Type Groups tab'.

fields.name: expenseTypeGroupEffectiveDatesFilter
fields.label: with effective dates
fields.sourceQuote: (Optional) Select the desired date range (all currently active, or all tax authorities) in the with effective dates list, then click Search.
fields.notes: Search filter on the Expense Types Group tab. The parenthetical 'all currently active, or all tax authorities' reads as a garbled description of the two choices; it is NOT recorded as a value set because the corpus does not present it as the option labels.

fields.name: expenseTypeGroupName
fields.label: Group Name
fields.sourceQuote: Enter the display name for the group.
fields.notes: Group Name step of the expense type group wizard.

fields.name: expenseTypeGroupEffectiveDate
fields.label: Effective Date
fields.sourceQuote: Select the effective date of the group.
fields.notes: Required. understand-and-use-the-effective-date-and-the-end-date-ccf72f26.md: 'When creating an expense type or vendor group you are required to enter an effective date during configuration.'

fields.name: expenseTypeGroupEndDate
fields.label: End Date
fields.sourceQuote: Typically, the system will set this date when it is time to retire this group. Leave this blank unless there is a specific end date you want to enforce.
fields.notes: Optional. Documented default when left blank is 12/31/9999 (understand-and-use-the-effective-date-and-the-end-date-ccf72f26.md).

fields.name: expenseTypeGroupAppliesTo
fields.label: Applies To
fields.sourceQuote: Select the Payment Request document type for which to calculate VAT for expense type groups.
fields.notes: The corpus names only 'Payment Request' as the document type and never enumerates the list, so validValues is deliberately empty. The setting also surfaces as a column on the Expense Type Groups page.

fields.name: expenseTypeGroupTaxCode
fields.label: Tax Code
fields.sourceQuote: The tax code can contain up to 20 characters. The Tax Code field is an arbitrary field and will be a read-only field for the user.
fields.notes: 20-character maximum, arbitrary value, read-only to the end user. 'VAT tax codes are applicable to invoices only.'

fields.name: expenseTypeGroupDisableVatCalculation
fields.label: Disable VAT calculation
fields.sourceQuote: If this is the case, select the check box to disable VAT calculation.
fields.notes: Explicitly a check box. Constraint: 'You can only disable VAT calculation for invoices.' Use case given is countries where vendors already supply VAT amounts, e.g. the UK.

fields.name: expenseTypeGroupExpenseTypes
fields.label: Expense Types
fields.sourceQuote: On the Expense Types step, select the desired expense types in the Expense Types column.
fields.notes: Values are the tenant's configured expense types (Expense Types page), so not enumerable from documentation.

fields.name: expenseTypeGroupUnavailableExpenseTypes
fields.label: Unavailable Expense Types
fields.sourceQuote: Any expense types that are already used for this tax authority appear in the Unavailable Expense Types pane with the name of the group.
fields.notes: Read-only pane. Exclusivity rule is scoped to one tax authority only - see availability-of-expense-types-based-on-location-of-tax-authority-8485155d.md.

fields.name: expenseTypeGroupTaxRateRateType
fields.label: Rate Type
fields.sourceQuote: The Tax Rates step shows the default tax condition of Always which means that this tax rate will always apply.
fields.notes: Tax Rates step of the expense type group wizard. Documented default tax condition is 'Always'. The Rate Type column list 'displays the rate types available for the selected tax authority'.

fields.name: vendorGroupTaxAuthorityFilter
fields.label: Tax Authority
fields.sourceQuote: On the Vendor Groups tab, select from the Tax Authority list.
fields.notes: Tab-level selector scoping every vendor group.

fields.name: vendorGroupEffectiveDatesFilter
fields.label: with effective dates
fields.sourceQuote: (Optional) Select the desired date range (all currently active, or all tax authorities) in the with effective dates list, and then click Search.
fields.notes: Vendor Groups twin of the expense type group filter. Wording differs only by 'and then click Search'.

fields.name: vendorGroupName
fields.label: Group Name
fields.sourceQuote: Enter the display name for the group.
fields.notes: Group Name step of the vendor group wizard. Read separately from step-5 rather than assumed identical.

fields.name: vendorGroupEffectiveDate
fields.label: Effective Date
fields.sourceQuote: Select the effective date of the group.
fields.notes: Required, same semantics as the expense type group.

fields.name: vendorGroupEndDate
fields.label: End Date
fields.sourceQuote: Typically, the system will set this date when it is time to retire this group. Leave this blank unless there is a specific end date you want to enforce.
fields.notes: Optional; blank means the documented 12/31/9999 default.

fields.name: vendorGroupAppliesTo
fields.label: Applies To
fields.sourceQuote: Select the Payment request document type for which to calculate VAT for vendor groups.
fields.notes: Note the casing drift: step-6 writes 'Payment request', step-5 writes 'Payment Request'. Also inherits step-6's own oddity - it says the setting appears as a column on the Expense Type Groups page, not the Vendor Groups page.

fields.name: vendorGroupTaxCode
fields.label: Tax Code
fields.sourceQuote: You can associate a tax code to a relevant set of vendors. This information will then feed into your financial system to make it easier for your company to handle tax.
fields.notes: 20-character maximum, read-only to the user, invoices only.

fields.name: vendorGroupDisableVatCalculation
fields.label: Disable VAT calculation
fields.sourceQuote: In countries where vendors already provide VAT amounts, for example in the UK, there might not be a need to perform VAT calculation.
fields.notes: Check box; 'You can only disable VAT calculation for invoices.'

fields.name: vendorGroupTaxType
fields.label: Tax Type
fields.sourceQuote: select a type of tax, international, domestic, taxable, etc., for this optional step, from the Tax Type list.
fields.notes: Optional, on the Vendor Name step. UNIQUE to the Vendor Groups tab - there is no counterpart on the Expense Types Group tab. 'international, domestic, taxable, etc.' is prose with an 'etc.', NOT a closed list, so validValues is empty. The Vendor Import template (tools-guides the-import-template-fields-and-descriptions-8b53850b.md) enumerates a Tax Type list of DITX/DNTX/INTX for VENDOR records - that is the Vendor Manager import, a different surface; it is recorded as a dependency, NOT copied onto this field.

fields.name: vendorGroupUnavailableVendors
fields.label: Unavailable Vendors
fields.sourceQuote: Any vendors that are already used for this tax authority appear in the Unavailable Vendors pane with the name of the group.
fields.notes: Read-only pane, vendor twin of Unavailable Expense Types.

fields.name: vendorGroupTaxRateRateType
fields.label: Rate Type
fields.sourceQuote: To change the rate type, click the field in the Rate Type column to select from the list, which displays the rate types available for the selected tax authority.
fields.notes: Tax Rates step of the vendor group wizard. Default tax condition documented as 'Always'.

fields.name: taxCodeName
fields.label: Tax Code (name)
fields.sourceQuote: Type the name of the code and then click Save.
fields.notes: Tax Code tab: click New, type the name, Save. Predefining codes converts the end user's tax code fields from read-only to a list: 'If the admin does not predefine tax codes, the user will see the tax codes in read-only fields and not in lists.' CONTRADICTION on the result: 6b42509f says 'the tax code fields (1-4)' become a list, be8bc5b8 says 'the VAT Tax Code 1 field'. Both recorded.

fields.name: taxValidationPartnerAccountNumber
fields.label: Partner Account Number
fields.sourceQuote: This is the unique account number provided by a tax service provider to the client. Enter this number in this field.
fields.notes: Tax Validation tab. LABEL CONTRADICTION: work-with-the-tax-validation-page-options-c3fe1df5.md calls the same control the 'Unique Tax Partner Number'. Both labels recorded; no reconciliation.

fields.name: taxValidationType
fields.label: Tax Validation Type
fields.sourceQuote: The service will perform the validation on the request type you specify here. Select Payment Request Only.
fields.notes: Only one documented value. c3fe1df5 confirms: 'At this time, only the Payment Request Only option is available.' and flags 'The Purchase Request type will be added to this feature in an upcoming service release.' - a future value, NOT recorded as current.

fields.name: taxValidationLevel
fields.label: Tax Validation Level
fields.sourceQuote: This defines on which level the tax validation should occur, either the Header or the Line Item level.
fields.notes: Values are taken from the field description's own enumeration, not from a separate list. LABEL CONTRADICTION: c3fe1df5 calls this 'Form Level to Be Analyzed' and describes the choice as 'Either the header or line item details form'.

fields.name: turnOnTaxValidation
fields.label: Turn On Tax Validation
fields.sourceQuote: Select (enable) to activate tax validation for the specified request type.
fields.notes: Ordering constraint stated in the field's own TIP: 'Do not activate the service until all configuration steps, such as expense type to commodity code mapping, are finalized.' This is the last step of the Tax Validation configuration.

fields.name: taxValidationExpenseTypes
fields.label: Expense Types
fields.sourceQuote: This list of expense types represents the client-defined expense types. It is provided to allow mapping to commodity codes and is read-only for this purpose.
fields.notes: Read-only. Sourced from the tenant's Expense Types configuration; exists only as the left side of the commodity-code mapping.

fields.name: unspscCommodityCode
fields.label: UNSPSC Commodity Code
fields.sourceQuote: The client can import the expense type to code mapping (Expense Type import) or adjust by clicking the text box directly and manually entering a new value.
fields.notes: Editable text box per expense type. Populated three ways: system import of the UN codes, the Expense Type import, or manual entry. c3fe1df5 adds '(Optional: You may also add these manually using options in the Tax Administration tool.)'

fields.name: unspscCommodityCodeSearch
fields.label: Search
fields.sourceQuote: A Search link is provided to open a browser to the latest UN commodity codes for accurate input.
fields.notes: Opens the United Nations Standard Products and Services Code (UNSPSC) page; described again in work-with-commodity-codes-in-this-view-f37c2a6e.md.

valueSetCandidates.context: Only one request type is currently offered by the Tax Validation service; the corpus explicitly says additional types are future work.
valueSetCandidates.sourceQuote: At this time, only the Payment Request Only option is available.
valueSetCandidates.notes: Do NOT add 'Purchase Request' - the corpus names it only as an upcoming release item.

valueSetCandidates.context: The only calculation method the corpus ever names for a tax rate type.
valueSetCandidates.sourceQuote: Select Percentage. This is the default choice.
valueSetCandidates.notes: Called the default, but no alternative is documented anywhere in the corpus. A second method must not be invented.

valueSetCandidates.context: Two levels enumerated inside the field description on the Tax Validation tab.
valueSetCandidates.sourceQuote: This defines on which level the tax validation should occur, either the Header or the Line Item level.
valueSetCandidates.notes: c3fe1df5 restates the same two options in lower case as 'header or line item details form'. Recorded as a value set because both members are explicitly named; the exact on-screen casing is undetermined.

notes: LENS FINDING, stated plainly: the tools-guides directory documents ZERO controls of the Tax Administration page itself. I exhausted it first - grep for 'tax authorit|tax administration|tax administrator|tax validation|tax code|expense type group|vendor group' across all 650 tools files returns only vendor-group/vendor-access topics (a different feature), a Mexican CFDi attachment topic, and working-with-tax-and-vat-data-f690215c.md, which is an audit-trail statement, not a control. What tools-guides DOES own for this domain is cross-cutting: the per-country VAT field implementation guidance (canada / uk-us-japan-australia / other-countries), the Switch Tax Mode end-user button, the OCR extraction raw <table>, and the Vendor Import Tax Type column. Those are recorded here as contradictions and dependencies, not as page fields. This page is therefore a genuine admin-guides-only page; the 23/337 tools-guides citation ratio does not improve from Tax Administration and should not be forced. UNDETERMINED: (1) uiVariant - no topic anywhere differentiates a new/legacy Tax Administration page, so every field is 'undifferentiated'. The only 'New User Experience' hit in the whole tax corpus is vat-at-header-and-line-item-level-8b39f76e.md, which describes an END-USER 'Display Tax' toggle in the Itemizations section, not an admin control - and value-added-tax-vat-8b39be89.md line 54 is revision history only. I did not read two matching variants of anything, so 'both' is claimed nowhere. (2) Country and State/Province lists are never enumerated. (3) The Applies To list is never enumerated - only 'Payment Request' is ever named. (4) 'with effective dates' option labels are never given cleanly. (5) Withholding tax: grep for 'withholding' returns ZERO files in BOTH guide directories - it is not documented in this corpus, and I have not invented a control for it. (6) The digital tax invoice statuses (Not validated / Valid / Valid with warnings / Invalid) are a genuine documented list but attach to a PROCESSOR-VISIBLE status on the invoice, not to any configuration field on this page, so they are deliberately NOT emitted as a valueSetCandidate - there is no field to wire them to. (7) I did not re-home available-vat-fields, extract-vat-data or configure-vat-labels: those are Forms and Fields form fields, already built; they appear here only in compressedRanges and dependencies. (8) 'exempt, standard, or reduced' and 'Standard or Reduced' are stated as EXAMPLES of rate type names and are not harvested as values.
